examples.japanese: それは{私|わたし}の{仕事|しごと}の{範疇|はんちゅう}ではない。
examples.english: That is not within the scope of my work.

examples.japanese: この{問題|もんだい}は{法律|ほうりつ}の{範疇|はんちゅう}に{入|はい}る。
examples.english: This issue falls within the domain of law.

examples.japanese: {許容|きょよう}できる{範疇|はんちゅう}を{超|こ}えた{行為|こうい}は{厳|きび}しく{処分|しょぶん}される。
examples.english: Actions that exceed the acceptable scope are strictly punished.

notes:
A formal word meaning a class or category of things, or the extent of a particular sphere. Originally a philosophical term borrowed from Chinese, now widely used in formal writing and speech to indicate whether something falls within or outside a particular classification.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {範疇|はんちゅう}に{入|はい}る: fall within the scope
- {範疇|はんちゅう}を{超|こ}える: exceed the scope
- {範疇|はんちゅう}に{含|ふく}まれる: be included in the category
- {範疇|はんちゅう}{外|がい}: outside the scope

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {範囲|はんい}: range, scope — more general and less formal
- {分野|ぶんや}: field, area — emphasizes the subject domain rather than boundaries
- カテゴリー: category — the loanword equivalent, used in casual contexts
